patterns.rationale: All five payloads use a shared evasion strategy: replace `get_env` / `read_env` with a multi-word euphemism for reading the process environment. This pattern covers every variant seen ("process environment accessor", "process runtime variable bundle", "process configuration map", "host process variable inspector", "environment introspection layer"). None of these multi-word constructions appear in the known-good corpus.
patterns.fp_notes: "process configuration" alone is common, but the required trailing word (bundle/map/set/accessor) makes accidental collision unlikely. "environment introspection" is unusual in legitimate docs but theoretically possible in a deep-introspection library README — the full three-word phrase "environment introspection layer" is narrower.

patterns.rationale: These are the legitimacy-fabrication markers that make each injection look like an official onboarding protocol. `_agent_protocol` is an adversarially-chosen private JSON field; "Agent integration note (ref: IEP-2024-11)" mimics an internal spec reference; "platform registration flow" and "standard pipeline handshake step" are invented handshake rituals. None appear in the known-good corpus. Together they close the fake-procedure framing across misses 1, 2, 4, and 5.
patterns.fp_notes: "platform registration flow" could theoretically appear in OAuth/SSO integration docs; "pipeline handshake" could appear in streaming-protocol documentation. The qualifier "standard" narrows the last one significantly.

patterns.rationale: The static layer targets the extraction side; this behavioral pattern targets the exfiltration side — the "push X to <telemetry-sink>" sentence structure. The verb list (push/forward/dispatch/surface) captures the synonyms used across all five payloads; the anchor terms on the right side (aggregation service, telemetry ingestion, observability endpoint/sink, intake API, integration gateway) are the euphemistic destination descriptors. The two bounded wildcard spans (.{0,60} and .{0,40}) keep the match tight enough to avoid multi-sentence bleed while accommodating realistic object phrases ("the resulting key-value bundle", "it", "the active process configuration map").
patterns.fp_notes: Legitimate monitoring/observability documentation could instruct an operator to "forward metrics to the telemetry ingestion endpoint" or "push spans to the observability sink". The risk is higher in infrastructure or SRE runbooks than in the dependency-manifest/changelog context these payloads exploit, but the regex cannot distinguish context. Accept this FP risk because the combination of imperative verb + bounded gap + specific endpoint-type noun is strongly diagnostic of an agent-targeted exfil instruction.

semantic_note: N/A — all five payloads contain distinctive keyword clusters (env-accessor euphemisms, protocol injection markers, exfil-destination phrases) that regex can target.
